body:
Depends on #593 (stack mode: append-only fold over the real PR branches). Found while re-planning #593.

## Defect

The goal is that one `pdca flow` command drives a whole milestone in stack mode. When a run stops part-way (an integrity stop, the pass budget, a crash, Ctrl-C), the recovery is to re-issue the same command. Today that resumed run builds dependents on a base that lacks their prerequisites:

- Bundles that finished in the earlier run are skipped as already terminal (`flow.py:2076`), so they are not in this run's batch and never enter `accepted` / the fold.
- With nothing folded yet, `_point_at_integration` clears the dependent's stack base (`flow.py:694-706`), so it is cut from the plain target base.
- `_runnable` accepts an out-of-batch prerequisite as ready once it is COMPLETE (`flow.py:681-683`). COMPLETE only means a draft PR was opened, so the prerequisite's work is not in the base unless that PR has merged. Only `Depends on (merged)` waits for the merge (#186).

Result: the dependent is built, checked and published against a tree missing its prerequisite. Nothing reports it.

## Expected

Re-issuing the same `pdca flow <ids>` after any stop continues the milestone correctly: every bundle builds on a base that carries all of its declared prerequisites.

## Suggested direction (after #593 lands)

Before the run's first wave, fold the published, still-unmerged branches of out-of-batch COMPLETE prerequisites of this run's bundles onto the integration line (#593's fold merges published branches, so this re-creates the earlier run's line from the same commits). Then point the dependents at that line as usual. A prerequisite that is COMPLETE but has no published branch holds its dependents (named on stderr), it does not let them build on the wrong base. A merged prerequisite needs nothing: its work is already in the base.
title: stack mode: a re-issued flow builds dependents of an earlier run's unmerged work on a base missing it
